messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

The user wants to retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius. We need to use the provided tool `functions.requests_get`. We need to call the Open-Meteo API. The user didn't specify coordinates. We need to find coordinates for White Plains. White Plains is a city in New York, USA. Coordinates: approx 41.0536° N, 73.7629° W. So latitude ~41.0536, longitude ~-73.7629.

We need to get forecast for next week. The Open-Meteo API supports daily forecasts. We can request daily temperature_min and temperature_max for the next 7 days. We need to set timezone. We can use "timezone=America/New_York". We need to set "start_date" and "end_date". For next week, we need to compute dates. Let's assume today is 2026-05-27. Next week would be 2026-06-03 to 2026-06-09? Actually next week could mean the upcoming week starting Monday after today. Today is Saturday. Next week might start Monday 2026-05-29. But it's ambiguous. We can interpret "next week" as the next 7 days from tomorrow. So from 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-03 inclusive. That covers 7 days. Or we can just request daily forecast for the next 7 days. The API can return daily data for the next 7 days if we don't specify start_date and end_date. But we can specify "forecast_days=7".

Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=America/New_York&forecast_days=7

We need to call the function. We'll pass the URL and params accordingly. The function signature expects "url" and "params" with keys: latitude, longitude, elevation. We also need to pass query parameters like daily, timezone, forecast_days. But the function's "params" only includes latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't allow arbitrary query parameters. However, the function description says "Query parameters for the GET request." It lists latitude, longitude, elevation. But we need to pass other query parameters. The function signature may not support them. But maybe we can pass them in the "params" field? The function signature only includes those three fields. But we can pass additional keys? The type definition shows only those keys. So we cannot pass daily, timezone, forecast_days. But maybe we can embed them in the URL? The "url" field is the full URL. We can construct the full URL with all query parameters. Then we don't need to use "params". The "params" field is optional. So we can just put the full URL with query parameters. That might be simpler.

Thus we will call:

URL: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=41.0536&longitude=-73.7629&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=America/New_York&forecast_days=7"

We can set headers to default. We can leave other fields default.
